alg-euler-maruyama-autonomous:
## Definition

Assume AC. Fix finite integers $d,m\ge1$, $T>0$, and $N\ge1$ such that
$h=T/N\le1$. Work on a filtered probability space whose filtration is
right-continuous and contains every $P$-null subset of $\mathcal F$ in
$\mathcal F_0$. Let $W$ be an adapted standard
$m$-dimensional Brownian motion whose increments after time $s$ are
independent of $\mathcal F_s$. Let $X_0$ be finite, $\mathcal F_0$-measurable,
and independent of $\sigma(W_t-W_0:0\le t\le T)$.
Let $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ and
$g:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^{d\times m}$ be $C^1$. Assume finite constants
$\mu,c,D\ge0$ and an integer $q\ge1$ satisfy, for all $x,y\in\mathbb R^d$,
$$ \langle x-y,f(x)-f(y)\rangle\le\mu|x-y|^2,\qquad \|g(x)-g(y)\|_F^2\le c|x-y|^2, $$
$$ |f(x)-f(y)|^2\le D(1+|x|^q+|y|^q)|x-y|^2. $$
Here $|\cdot|$ is the Euclidean norm and $\|\cdot\|_F$ is the Frobenius
norm.

Set $t_k=kh$ and construct the grid approximation recursively by
$$ Y_0=X_0,\qquad Y_{k+1}=Y_k+f(Y_k)h+g(Y_k)(W_{t_{k+1}}-W_{t_k}),\quad 0\le k<N. $$
The output also includes the left-endpoint step process
$$ \bar Y_t=Y_k\quad(t_k\le t<t_{k+1}),\qquad \bar Y_T=Y_N, $$
and the continuous interpolation
$$ Y_t=Y_k+f(Y_k)(t-t_k)+g(Y_k)(W_t-W_{t_k})\quad(t_k\le t\le t_{k+1}). $$
The recursion makes the two interpolation formulas agree at every shared
endpoint. The finite recursion is defined pathwise: $C^1$ coefficients are
finite-valued, each $Y_k$ is finite almost surely by induction, and Brownian
paths are continuous. This algorithm defines no moment or convergence claim.
lem-brownian-ito-integral-l1-maximal-bou:
## Statement

Assume AC. Work on a complete filtered probability space
$(\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{0\le t\le T},P)$ whose filtration is
right-continuous and contains every $P$-null subset of $\mathcal F$ in
$\mathcal F_0$. Let $m\ge1$ be finite, let
$W=(W^1,\dots,W^m)$ be an adapted standard $m$-dimensional Brownian motion
[[def-d-dimensional-brownian-motion]] whose increments after time $s$ are
independent of $\mathcal F_s$, and let $H=(H^1,\dots,H^m)$ be a predictable
row-vector process [[def-progressively-measurable-and-predictable-process]] with
$\mathbb E\int_0^T\|H_s\|_2^2ds<\infty$. For
$$ M_t=\sum_{j=1}^m\int_0^tH_s^j\,dW_s^j, $$
the continuous version satisfies
$$ \mathbb E\sup_{0\le t\le T}|M_t| \le16\sqrt m\,\mathbb E\left(\int_0^T\|H_s\|_2^2ds\right)^{1/2}. $$
lem-euler-maruyama-autonomous-interpolat:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice, let $d,m\ge1$ be finite, and fix $T>0$. Let
$f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ and $g:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^{d\times m}$ be
autonomous coefficients. Assume that, for constants $c,D\ge0$ and an integer
$q\ge1$,
$$ \|g(x)-g(y)\|_F^2\le c|x-y|^2, \qquad |f(x)-f(y)|^2\le D(1+|x|^q+|y|^q)|x-y|^2. $$
For each $0<h\le1$ with $N=T/h$ a positive integer, let $Y^h$ be the
continuous Euler–Maruyama interpolation and $\bar Y^h$ its left-endpoint step
process from [[alg-euler-maruyama-autonomous]].
Assume that for every finite $p\ge1$,
$$ \sup_{0<h\le1,\ T/h\in\mathbb N} \left(\mathbb E\sup_{t\le T}|Y_t^h|^p+ \mathbb E\sup_{t\le T}|\bar Y_t^h|^p\right)<\infty. $$
Then for every even integer $r\ge2$ there is a finite constant $C_r$, independent
of $h$, such that
$$ \sup_{0\le t\le T}\mathbb E|Y_t^h-\bar Y_t^h|^r\le C_r h^{r/2}. $$
The premise is an all-moment premise for this autonomous coefficient class; it
does not follow from the finite-$L^2$ moment bound alone.
thm-euler-maruyama-strong-rate-under-hig:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $d,m\ge1$ be finite, fix $T>0$, and work on a complete filtered
probability space whose filtration is right-continuous and contains every
$P$-null subset of $\mathcal F$ in $\mathcal F_0$. Let $W=(W_t)_{0\le t\le T}$
be an adapted standard $m$-dimensional Brownian motion whose increments are
independent of the current filtration. Let
$X_0$ be finite and $\mathcal F_0$-measurable, independent of
$\sigma(W_t-W_0:0\le t\le T)$. Use Euclidean state norms and the Frobenius
matrix norm. Consider
the autonomous SDE
$$ X_t=X_0+\int_0^t f(X_s)\,ds+\int_0^t g(X_s)\,dW_s, \qquad X_t\in\mathbb R^d, $$
where $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ and
$g:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^{d\times m}$ are $C^1$. Assume that constants
$\mu,c,D\ge0$ and an integer $q\ge1$ satisfy, for all $x,y\in\mathbb R^d$,
$$ \langle x-y,f(x)-f(y)\rangle\le\mu|x-y|^2, \qquad \|g(x)-g(y)\|_F^2\le c|x-y|^2, $$
and
$$ |f(x)-f(y)|^2\le D(1+|x|^q+|y|^q)|x-y|^2. $$
For each $0<h\le1$ with $N=T/h\in\mathbb N$, let $Y^h$ be the continuous
Euler–Maruyama interpolation and $\bar Y^h$ its left-endpoint step process
from [[alg-euler-maruyama-autonomous]]. Assume
that an exact strong solution $X$ and these exact, step and continuous Euler
processes have uniformly bounded moments of every finite order on $[0,T]$:
for every $p\ge1$,
$$ \mathbb E\sup_{t\le T}|X_t|^p+ \sup_{0<h\le1,\ T/h\in\mathbb N}\left( \mathbb E\sup_{t\le T}|Y_t^h|^p+ \mathbb E\sup_{t\le T}|\bar Y_t^h|^p\right)<\infty. $$
Then a constant $C$, independent of $h$, satisfies
$$ \mathbb E\sup_{0\le t\le T}|X_t-Y_t^h|^2\le Ch. $$
In particular the grid-point root-mean-square error is $O(h^{1/2})$.
The all-moment premise is part of this source contract; $X_0\in L^2$ alone
does not imply it.
thm-euler-maruyama-strong-rate-for-squar:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d,m\ge1$ be finite, fix $T>0$, and work on
the complete usual filtered probability space of
[[def-ito-sde-and-strong-solution]]. Let $0<h\le1$ with $N=T/h\in\mathbb N$.
Use Euclidean state norms and the Frobenius matrix norm. Let $W$ be an adapted
standard $m$-dimensional Brownian motion whose increments are independent of
the current filtration. Let
$b:[0,T]\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ and
$\sigma:[0,T]\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^{d\times m}$ be jointly Borel,
and suppose finite nonnegative constants $L,K$ satisfy, for all $s,t\in[0,T]$ and
$x,y\in\mathbb R^d$,
$$ |b(t,x)-b(t,y)|+\|\sigma(t,x)-\sigma(t,y)\|_F\le L|x-y|, $$
$$ |b(t,x)|^2+\|\sigma(t,x)\|_F^2\le K^2(1+|x|^2), $$
and
$$ |b(t,x)-b(s,x)|+\|\sigma(t,x)-\sigma(s,x)\|_F \le K(1+|x|)|t-s|^{1/2}. $$
Let $X_0$ be $\mathcal F_0$-measurable, independent of
$\sigma(W_t-W_0:0\le t\le T)$, with $\mathbb E|X_0|^2<\infty$. Let $X$ be the exact continuous
strong solution with
$$ \mathbb E\sup_{t\le T}|X_t|^2<\infty, $$
and let $Y^h,\bar Y^h$ be the continuous Euler interpolation and left-endpoint
step process of
[[def-euler-maruyama-step-process-and-continuous-interpolation]]. The
uniform pointwise moment and interpolation-increment bounds of
[[thm-euler-maruyama-uniform-moment-and-increment-bounds]] then imply that a
constant $C$, independent of $h$, satisfies
$$ \mathbb E\sup_{0\le t\le T}|X_t-Y_t^h|^2\le Ch. $$
Thus the grid-point root-mean-square error is $O(h^{1/2})$. The constant may
depend on $T,d,m,L,K$ and the exact-solution supremum-moment bound supplied by
the P-SDE-01 existence theorem.
thm-euler-maruyama-weak-order-one-under-:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d,m\ge1$ be finite, fix $T>0$, and work on
the complete usual filtered probability space of
[[def-ito-sde-and-strong-solution]]. Take $0<h\le1$ with $N=T/h\in\mathbb N$.
Let $W$ be an adapted standard
$m$-dimensional Brownian motion with increments independent of the current
filtration. Use Euclidean state norms and the Frobenius matrix norm, and write
$A:B=\operatorname{tr}(A^{\mathsf T}B)$. Let
$b:[0,T]\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ and
$\sigma:[0,T]\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^{d\times m}$ be jointly Borel,
globally Lipschitz in state, of uniform linear growth, and satisfy the
half-Hölder time modulus in [[alg-euler-maruyama]]. Let $X_0$ be
$\mathcal F_0$-measurable, independent of $\sigma(W_t-W_0:0\le t\le T)$, with
$\mathbb E|X_0|^p<\infty$ for some $p\ge2q+8$, where $q\ge0$ is finite;
when $q=0$, use the convention $|x|^q=1$.
Let $X$ be the exact strong solution and $Y^h,\bar Y^h$ the continuous
Euler interpolation and step process of
[[def-euler-maruyama-step-process-and-continuous-interpolation]].

For a bounded Borel payoff $\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$, define
$$ u(t,x)=\mathbb E\bigl[\varphi(X_T^{t,x})\bigr], $$
where $X^{t,x}$ is the unique shifted strong solution started from $x$ at time
$t$, supplied by [[thm-global-strong-well-posedness-for-lipschitz-ito-sdes]]. Set
$$ L_t v(x)=b(t,x)\cdot\nabla v(x)+\tfrac12\bigl(\sigma(t,x)\sigma(t,x)^{\mathsf T}\bigr):D_x^2v(x). $$
Assume $u(T,x)=\varphi(x)$ and $(\partial_t+L_t)u=0$ on
$[0,T)\times\mathbb R^d$. A multi-index is $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_d)$
with nonnegative integer entries and $|\alpha|=\sum_i\alpha_i$. Assume every
mixed derivative
$\partial_t^jD_x^\alpha u$ with $0\le j\le2$ and $|\alpha|\le4$ exists,
is continuous, and satisfies
$$ |\partial_t^jD_x^\alpha u(t,x)|\le C_u(1+|x|^q) $$
for a common constant $C_u$. Finally, assume the exact and Euler processes
have uniform pointwise moments of order $p$ on $[0,T]$; the Euler bounds are
provided by [[thm-euler-maruyama-uniform-moment-and-increment-bounds]] and the
exact bound by the P-SDE-01 moment contract. Then
$$ \bigl|\mathbb E\varphi(X_T)-\mathbb E\varphi(Y_N^h)\bigr|\le C h, $$
where $C$ is independent of $h$. The theorem is conditional on the stated
backward regularity; it does not derive that regularity from coefficient or
payoff smoothness.
thm-shared-brownian-euler-level-correcti:
## Statement

Assume AC and the finite-$L^2$ coefficient and initial-value hypotheses of
[[thm-euler-maruyama-strong-rate-for-square-integrable-initial-data]]. Fix an
integer refinement factor $M\ge2$ and a fine step $h$ with $0<h\le1/M$,
$T/h\in\mathbb N$, and $T/(Mh)\in\mathbb N$. Construct the fine and coarse
Euler paths with the same initial value and Brownian motion. The coarse
Brownian increment over each coarse interval is, by definition, the sum of
the $M$ fine Brownian increments in that interval. Let $X_T$ be the common
exact solution, and let $\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ be globally
Lipschitz with constant $L_\varphi$. Then constants independent of $h$ satisfy
$$ \mathbb E|Y_T^h-Y_T^{Mh}|^2\le C_M h, $$
$$ \operatorname{Var}\bigl(\varphi(Y_T^h)-\varphi(Y_T^{Mh})\bigr)\le C_ML_\varphi^2h, \qquad |\mathbb E\varphi(X_T)-\mathbb E\varphi(Y_T^h)|\le C L_\varphi h^{1/2}. $$
Thus the Lipschitz-payoff Euler level pair has correction variance exponent
$\beta=1$ and strong-error bias exponent $\alpha=1/2$. If, in addition,
$\varphi$ is bounded and its backward value function satisfies the hypotheses
of [[thm-euler-maruyama-weak-order-one-under-backward-regularity]], then the
bias bound improves to $|\mathbb E\varphi(X_T)-\mathbb E\varphi(Y_T^h)|\le Ch$,
so $\alpha=1$ while $\beta=1$ remains. With fixed dimension, fixed $M$, and
unit-cost coefficient and payoff evaluations, one coupled fine/coarse sample
has work $O(h^{-1})$.
